reviews.body: Almost there. Could you also update the description? It still describes the first version.

review_comments.body: Why these three classes? No other command sorts errors this way. Cannot we just catch the known failures where they happen, like `getRedocOptions` does, and drop this `catch`, so the wrapper prints the rest with the stack?
This test has more mocks than the actual testing. Is there a description that reproduces the `TypeError`? Then it could be an e2e test in `tests/e2e/build-docs`.

This doesn't seem right. A description with invalid YAML or an unreachable URL now prints as an unexpected error with a stack. Cannot we just use `handleError` around the loading, like [here](https://github.com/Redocly/redocly-cli/blob/23321f1a22e5bf54ae42ed5b133a0372549e5a2c/packages/cli/src/commands/bundle.ts#L190)?
No need in these two, the snapshot already shows both.
Do we need a changeset here? The error shows itself, and it's rather a chore than a fix.

Thanks, that is cleaner. I dropped the `catch` in `handlerBuildCommand`, so unexpected errors reach the wrapper and print with their stack. The one known failure I handle where it happens is an unreadable `--template` file (now a `HandledError` with a short message, as `getRedocOptions` does). I replaced the mock-based unit test with an e2e test in `tests/e2e/build-docs` (missing template: short message, no "unexpected error"). I could not find a description that reproduces the `TypeError` from #3054 (the reporter could not share theirs), so that case has no test of its own.
